title: Generic stalk of the structure sheaf under a finite dominant morphism
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be integral schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] whose image is dense in $Y$. Write $\eta_X,\eta_Y$ for their generic points [def-sc-generic-point], and $k(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}$ and $k(Y)=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$ for their function fields [def-sc-function-field]. Equip $k(X)$ with the canonical $k(Y)$-algebra structure of the dominant morphism [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Let $\mathcal F=f_*\mathcal O_X$ be the sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras defined on an open $V\subseteq Y$ by $\mathcal F(V)=\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_X)$. Its stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] at $\eta_Y$ is a $k(Y)$-algebra. The canonical map
$$\mathcal F_{\eta_Y}\longrightarrow k(X),$$
which sends the germ of a section over $f^{-1}V$ to its germ at $\eta_X$, is an isomorphism of $k(Y)$-algebras. No smoothness, normality, flatness, dimension, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AYZ (lemma-degree-pullback-map-proper-curves), first sentence of the proof identifying the generic rank of the finite direct image with the function-field degree; the generic-stalk comparison used there, for finite dominant morphisms of integral schemes.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ of $\eta_Y$. Finiteness makes $U=f^{-1}V$ affine. Apply [lem-sfb-dominant-affine-germ-comparison]: with $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)$, $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$, $\varphi:A\to B$, $C=(f_*\mathcal O_X)_{\eta_Y}$ and its maps $j_A,j_B,\iota,\sigma,c,\alpha$, both rings are domains, $\varphi$ is injective, the generic prime of $V$ is zero, and $k(X)$ is the fraction field of $B$ through $j_B$. This lemma also gives $c\iota=j_B$ and $c\sigma=\alpha$.

proof.text:
By [lem-sc-affine-pushforward-stalk-localization], the actual germ map $\iota:B	o C$ localizes $B$ at $S=\varphi(A\setminus\{0\})$: its affine-morphism hypothesis follows from finiteness, and its target prime is zero by step 1. Thus every element of $C$ has the form $\iota(b)\iota(\varphi(a))^{-1}$ with $a
e0$. For $a
e0$, injectivity of $\varphi$ and $j_B$ gives $j_B(\varphi(a))
e0$. Since $c\iota=j_B$, the image of that fraction is $j_B(b)j_B(\varphi(a))^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence, proof: affine stalk calculation.

proof.text: Finite implies integral by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]. The affine monic-equation condition in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] therefore applies to $A\to B$. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-localization-fraction-comparison] with this injection, $S=\varphi(A\setminus\{0\})$, the actual localization $\iota:B\to C$ of step 2 and the injective fraction map $j=j_B:B\to k(X)$ of step 1. It makes its specified comparison $q:C\to k(X)$ bijective. For each $b\in B$ and $a\ne0$, its formula and step 2 give $q(\iota(b)\iota(\varphi(a))^{-1})=j_B(b)j_B(\varphi(a))^{-1}=c(\iota(b)\iota(\varphi(a))^{-1})$. Every element has this form. Also both ring maps extend $j_B$, since $c\iota=j_B$ by step 1; hence the uniqueness clause of the same lemma identifies $q=c$. Thus the canonical germ map $c$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 00GS, lemma-integral-over-field (2), algebraic background for the localized domain being a field. The explicit monic-equation inverse certificate and comparison with a specified fraction field are the agent expansion of old proof steps 5-6, rather than a formula quoted from this tag.

proof.text: The scalar map for $C$ is $\sigma$, and the prescribed scalar map for $k(X)$ is $\alpha$. Step 1 gives $c\sigma=\alpha$ through the actual germ maps. Thus $c(\sigma(h)z)=\alpha(h)c(z)$ for $h\in k(Y)$ and $z\in C$. By step 3 let $t$ be the inverse of $c$. Applying $c$ and its injectivity gives $t(\alpha(h)w)=\sigma(h)t(w)$ for $w\in k(X)$: both sides map to $\alpha(h)w$. The same argument with sums, products and $1$ shows that $t$ is a unital ring map. Hence the actual canonical comparison and its inverse are maps of the prescribed $k(Y)$-algebras, as required.
